title: Sales Enablement Manager
description:
Ready to be a Titan? 
 This Sales Enablement Manager is a strategic orchestration role serving major GTM initiatives across our Upsell and Fintech organization This role will own enablement strategy across high-priority, cross-functional initiatives in addition to day-to-day enablement deliverables, including onboarding content, training sessions, and stakeholder communications. 
 This role is measured on the standard enablement fundamentals — scorecard-driven coaching and performance improvement for the team it supports — and, just as heavily, on how well it orchestrates change across the Upsell functions: product releases, pricing and process changes, and system changes that ripple across Sales Enablement, Product Marketing, RevOps, Post-Sales, Demand Gen, and Upsell leadership. Rollout success itself counts as performance here — the effectiveness and impact of a change to the function, not just that it shipped. The person in this seat runs the intake, prioritization, and enablement planning process for these initiatives (including the weekly Enablement Planning forum with business partners), decides what level of enablement effort a given change warrants, and makes sure the right stakeholders are aligned before, during, and after rollout. 
 What you'll do: 
 Initiative orchestration & strategy 
 Own intake, prioritization, and sequencing for high-priority Upsell initiatives — product releases, pricing/process changes, and system changes — using an impact-tiering framework (major/minor/minimal) to determine the right level of enablement effort for each. 
 Facilitate the recurring enablement planning forum with Upsell business partners (Sales Enablement, Product Marketing, RevOps, Post-Sales, Demand Gen, Sales/Engineering) to align on upcoming changes, timelines, and success criteria before rollout. 
 Build and maintain enablement plans for Tier 1 initiatives: problem, solution, success criteria, timeline, and stakeholder alignment, documented for reference. 
 Process & product change management 
 Translate product releases and process changes into what IC’s and managers need to know, do differently, and be measured on — then build the training, documentation, and communications to get them there. 
 Own change management and internal communications strategy for the function, based on the actual level of change management impact. 
 Partner with Product and Product Marketing to shape go-to-market requirements and adoption programs from an enablement lens, not just react to them after launch. 
 Training delivery & content creation 
 Build thoughtful, effective enablement content — training materials, playbooks, aids — not just orchestrate who else builds it, partnering with functional SMEs and stakeholders on subject-matter accuracy. 
 Deliver training directly for high-priority initiatives when it's the right vehicle (instructor-led sessions, working sessions with subject matter experts & managers), rather than handing delivery off entirely to stakeholders. 
 Cross-functional partnership 
 Serve as the enablement point of contact for Upsell leadership, GTM, Post Sales Functions, Fintech sellers, and product/revenue leaders on anything that touches how Upsell teams sell or operate. 
 Represent enablement's perspective in cross-functional planning so initiatives land with the right sequencing, training, and change management — not enablement as an afterthought. 
 Performance & measurement 
 Track adoption and effectiveness of major initiatives against the Upsell scorecard (readiness, adoption, effectiveness) and flag gaps or risks honestly rather than after the fact. 
 Continuously refine the intake and tiering process itself based on what did and didn't work on past rollouts. 
 What you'll bring: 
 Proven enablement experience, with demonstrated impact on business outcomes in a high-growth, fast-changing organization. 
 Deep knowledge of the home services industry and ServiceTitan's product, platform, and customer base — able to speak credibly to what ServiceTitan sell and who they sell to. 
 Sales or account management experience, ideally in a B2B SaaS or post-sales motion, in addition to enablement experience. 
 BA/BS degree and 4-6+ years of related experience in enablement, training, or GTM program management. 
 Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent, cross-functional initiatives — running intake, prioritization, and stakeholder alignment without a lot of oversight. 
 Strong track record building and maintaining relationships with senior stakeholders across Product, Product Marketing, RevOps, and Sales/Account Management leadership. 
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate product and process change into clear, action-oriented enablement for frontline teams and managers. 
 Ability to prioritize and sequence competing high-priority initiatives in a fast-paced, sometimes ambiguous environment. 
 Proficiency with CRMs, LMS platforms, eLearning software, and project tracking tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence). 
 Experience in people management or a demonstrated ability to motivate and lead others without direct authority. 
 Be Human With Us: 
Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us. 
 Use of AI Technology: 
We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams.
 What We Offer: 
When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career:
 Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work : Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more.
 Holistic health and wellness benefits: Company-paid medical, dental, and vision (with 100% employer paid options and 90% coverage for dependents), FSA and HSA, 401k match, and telehealth options including memberships to One Medical.
 Support for Titans at all stages of life: Parental leave and support, up to $20k in fertility services (i.e. IUI and IVF), surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement, on demand maternity support through Maven Maternity, free breast milk shipping through Maven Milk, pet insurance, legal advisory services, financial planning tools, and more.

title: Sales Compensation Manager
description:
Hello. We’re Teya. 
Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.
They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.
 Teya exists to change that. 
We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.
We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.
If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you
 Become a part of our story. 
Teya is building out its Commercial Planning & Performance team, which will be the analytical backbone of our commercial organisation. We're looking for a Sales Compensation Manager to own the central planning machine across our long-range plan, annual budget, and quarterly target-setting.
This is a specialist, individual-contributor role for someone who can build a stable, scalable commission framework, one that drives the right commercial behaviour, holds up economically, and can be operated consistently across countries. Good incentive design is part analytics, part judgement, part communication, and part discipline; you'll need all four. The role will be instrumental to design the model, test it against the economics, govern how it changes, and make sure the business can actually run it. You’ll partner closely with the local revenue operations teams in each country, as well as the Sales Leaders and People team to drive execution.
 What you'll do 
Design commission models across channels that support our commercial strategy and the behaviours we want to reward; simple enough for the field to understand and trust, and grounded in unit economics rather than headline rates.
Backtest plans against historical cohorts and current pricing, assessing the impact on CAC, monetisation, payback and retention before changes go live, and surfacing where the model needs adjustment.
Own the governance layer including the review and approval process for compensation changes, the policies and controls behind it, version control and clear communication. Hold the line against ad hoc tweaks that damage credibility with sales teams.
Build the reporting that tracks compensation outcomes by channel, cohort and country, monitoring whether incentives are driving the intended performance, and flagging distortion or gaming risks early.
Coordinate rollout and implementation with country teams, Finance, payroll and operations, translating plan design into practical rules, supporting field communication, and making sure the monthly commission cycle is reliable and auditable.
Partner closely with Pricing and other relevant stakeholders.
 What we're looking for 
Background in sales compensation, revenue operations, strategic finance, commercial operations, or consulting with exposure to pricing, incentives or GTM design.
Strong analytical and modelling skills where you can build a scheme, backtest it against historical cohorts, and forecast its cost and behavioural impact from first principles.
Commercial judgement, not just operational instinct. You understand what actually drives rep behaviour, and you design incentives that reward the right things without creating distortion.
Structured, detail-oriented, disciplined about documentation, change control, and holding a stable framework rather than over-tuning it.
Excellent communication; you can explain a comp plan to a sales rep and a CFO and have both trust it.
High discretion handling sensitive compensation data.
 A plus 
Experience in multi-country sales organisations.
Exposure to field sales, partner sales or inside sales incentive models.
Hands-on experience backtesting compensation against historical performance.
Familiarity with pricing and unit economics in payments, fintech, SaaS or another transaction-led business.

Health and Life Insurance.
Pension Scheme.
25 days of Annual Leave (+ Bank Holidays).

Office snacks every day.

title: Director, GTM & Revenue Operations
description:
THE CARWOW GROUP
 Carwow Group is driven by a passion for getting people into cars. But not just any car, the right car. That’s why we are building the go-to destination for car-changing, whether you are looking to buy, sell or lease. Designed to reach drivers everywhere with our trail-blazing portfolio of personality rich automotive brands; Carwow, Auto Express, evo, Driving Electric and Car Buyer.
What started as a simple reviews site, is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service. Over 10m customers have used Carwow to help them buy and sell cars since its inception.
In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia, doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with over 1.1 billion annual views, sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.
 WHY JOIN US?
 We are winners of the prestigious Culture 100 award that recognises the most loved and happiest tech companies to work for! We have just raised $52m in funding led by global venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners (an early backer of LinkedIn and Shopify) to accelerate our growth plans!
As pioneers, we’re always driving for new territory and positive change, so our work as a group is never done. Where others see difficulty, it’s our responsibility to see possibility – building new experiences, launching new titles and listening to drivers.
Being a part of Carwow Group means championing drivers and the automotive industry, acting as a disrupter and never being afraid to fail (but learning fast when we do!).
Our team of 600 employees across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal are revolutionising car-changing and we are fast expanding our mission across every single brand and country we operate in, so jump in!
 THE ROLE
 This is a director role running the operating engine behind our commercial teams. Carwow sells cars in two ways: Sell My Car, where drivers sell their car to dealers, and Get Your Car, where they buy or lease their next one. As Director, GTM & Revenue Operations you own the operating model those commercial teams run on: the go-to-market process, the enablement and quality that get people productive, the systems they work in (Salesforce and the wider commercial tech stack), the analytics that forecast the commercial number, and the programme management that lands cross-functional change. The function covers five areas: GTM Operations, Sales Enablement, Tooling & Platform, Rev-Ops Analytics and Program Management. You report to the VP, Marketplace Operations and sit close to both the numbers and the commercial teams you serve. You make the commercial motion work; the commercial teams own the selling and the relationships.
This is a builder's role as much as a running one. You inherit a team of three (programme management, sales enablement and platform) and a clear mandate to grow the function to what the business needs. Shaping and hiring that team, and making the case for it, is central to the job. The commercial org has recently brought its Sell My Car and Get Your Car teams into a single account-management function serving one dealer network, so you'll run one operating model across both products (a unified Salesforce, aligned targets and comp, consistent enablement and quality) and get the last of that integration to steady state. The function has already moved real numbers here, reworking the sales process, standing up sales-engagement tooling and sharpening enablement, and your job is to take that further.
You own the operating model, process, enablement, the systems requirement and the forecast. The commercial organisation owns the relationships, the selling and delivery against the number. You design the targets, compensation and territory structures with commercial leadership and you shape decisions through the strength of the operating case. In your first year, success looks like a forecast that's trusted and accurate, new hires productive faster, a consistent quality bar across the combined team, and the platform and process the org runs on every day.
 WHAT YOU’LL DO
 You will own the commercial operating model and the team that runs it, working hand in glove with the commercial organisation, Workforce Management, the trading leads, and the analytics and data teams that support the whole function.
Own GTM operations: define the go-to-market playbook, pipeline and commercial process across both marketplaces, and, with commercial leadership, design the targets, compensation and territory / account structures that tie individual attainment to the business outcome. Own capacity and headcount planning with Workforce Management.
Own sales enablement and quality: build the onboarding and ramp-to-productivity structures, a standard readiness sign-off, org-wide QA and calibration, and ongoing L&D for both individual contributors and leaders, so new hires get productive faster and quality holds across the organisation.
Own the requirements for the commercial systems and tooling: direct Salesforce as the commercial system of record, owning the process and workflow design, prioritisation and the roadmap to bring the whole commercial org onto one platform, plus the sales-engagement and automation tooling (e.g. Groove), AI-assisted workflows and the performance dashboards the teams run on. You own the requirement and how the commercial org runs on the platform; the platform itself, its build and administration, sits with the tech org, who you partner with and direct.
Own revenue-operations analytics and forecasting: produce a forward-looking commercial forecast that feeds trading and reconciles to Finance's P&L view, own the operational reporting that diagnoses what the volume and operational teams are driving into the number, and provide the evidence base behind comp and performance decisions. Run the combined Sell My Car and Get Your Car commercial operation as one, a single dealer view, one operating model, and consistent process across both products.

Chaos is a leading global software company that provides world-class visualization and design solutions, empowering creative minds to bring ideas to life.
For over twenty years, Chaos has developed innovative technologies serving multiple industries, including architecture and design, media and entertainment, and product e-commerce. Chaos’ solutions help architects, designers, VFX artists/animators, and other creative professionals share ideas, optimize workflows, and create immersive experiences.

 The Sales Enablement Manager is responsible for developing and executing the sales enablement programme across the global sales organisation. The role translates product capability and market positioning into practical tools, methodologies, and training that equip sellers and channel partners to engage effectively, reduce ramp time, and contribute to consistent revenue growth. Working closely with Sales, Product Marketing, and Channel, this role supports a cohesive, value-based narrative across all sales motions. This role requires a commercially grounded enablement professional with a clear track record in B2B SaaS sales environments with a strong grasp of the AEC or adjacent technology landscape being a plus.
 Main Responsibilities
Develop and maintain a value-based sales methodology that translates complex product capabilities into clear business outcomes, equipping sellers to engage effectively at every stage of the sales cycle.
Develop and maintain sales playbooks, talk tracks, objection handling guides, and competitive positioning materials that reflect current market conditions and product positioning.
Collaborate with Product Marketing to define and refine ideal customer profiles, buyer personas, and pain-point frameworks, ensuring GTM alignment across direct and partner sales channels.
Build and execute a structured onboarding programme for new sellers and channel partners, with a clear focus on reducing time-to-productivity and building foundational product and sales competency.
Design and deliver ongoing training and coaching programmes that develop advanced discovery, negotiation, and value-selling skills across the sales organisation.
Partner with Sales leadership to identify skill gaps, analyse pipeline and conversion data, and translate findings into targeted enablement interventions.
Track and report on enablement effectiveness, measuring the impact of training initiatives and sales plays on pipeline progression and revenue outcomes.

Manage the enablement content library and tooling, ensuring materials are current, accessible, and consistently used across the sales organisation.
 Job Requirements
 Required Experience
At least 5 years of experience in sales enablement within a B2B SaaS or technology company, with direct involvement in designing and delivering programmes that measurably improved sales performance.
Proven track record of building or contributing to a sales enablement programme, including playbook development, onboarding design, and ongoing coaching frameworks.
Demonstrable experience working embedded within or alongside a sales organisation: with a clear understanding of how enterprise or mid-market sales cycles work, what sellers need to win, and how enablement creates commercial impact.
Experience collaborating closely with Product Marketing to develop value messaging, ICP frameworks, and sales narratives.
Plus: Strong familiarity with the AEC, visualisation, or adjacent technology sectors; ability to develop credible technical fluency in complex software environments is required.
 Required Skills
Clear understanding of how B2B revenue is generated, where deals are won or lost, and how to design enablement that addresses real sales challenges rather than generic training need.
Able to take complex product capabilities or technical differentiators and translate them into compelling, outcome-focused narratives that resonate with both technical and executive buyers.
Demonstrated ability to design and deliver structured enablement programmes with clear learning objectives, measurable outcomes, and practical application to live deals.
Comfortable using pipeline data, sales performance metrics, and field insights to identify skill gaps, prioritise interventions, and demonstrate enablement impact.
Able to build effective working relationships across Sales, Product Marketing, and Channel without direct authority, driving alignment across competing priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication in English.

title: Revenue Operations Lead
description:
AI Revenue Engine Lead 
 About the Role 
We’re hiring a senior operator to find and fix the highest-impact problems in Better Health’s revenue engine.
Your mandate is simple: find where the funnel is broken and make it better. 
You’ll work across the entire revenue journey, from lead generation through enrollment, documentation, shipment, and recurring revenue. You’ll use data to identify bottlenecks and opportunities, get to the root cause, and then own the solution end-to-end.
This is a hands-on role. You won’t just diagnose problems or make recommendations. You’ll redesign processes, leverage AI and automation, improve systems, and lead cross-functional projects through implementation and measurable results.
You’ll report to the SVP of Strategy and Operations and work directly with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Operations, RCM, Finance, Product, and Engineering on some of the company’s highest-priority growth problems.
 What You’ll Do 
 Find and Fix Revenue Problems 
Continuously audit the revenue funnel to identify conversion gaps, bottlenecks, broken handoffs, manual work, and opportunities for growth.
Use data to get to the root cause of performance problems and prioritize opportunities based on business impact.
Own high-priority initiatives end-to-end, from defining the problem and developing the solution through implementation and measuring results.
Redesign processes and workflows rather than accepting “this is how we’ve always done it.”
Use AI and automation aggressively where they can improve conversion, prioritization, speed, visibility, or team productivity.
 Run the Revenue Engine 
Own the weekly revenue operating cadence, including funnel performance, forecasting, key drivers, risks, and actions.
Build the analytics and leading indicators that help us understand where performance is headed and why.
Maintain a consistent view of the funnel and ensure teams are working from trusted data and definitions.
Own CRM and revenue systems governance, while partnering with other teams on larger systems and technical implementations.
 Drive Cross-Functional Execution 
Turn ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses, workplans, owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Bring together the right people across functions and drive projects forward without waiting for perfect information or organizational structure.
Pressure-test assumptions, make recommendations, and hold teams accountable for execution.
Measure whether changes actually worked and iterate quickly when they didn’t.
 What You’ll Bring 
8+ years of experience building and operating businesses, ideally across high-growth startups, strategy & operations, revenue operations, consulting, product, or similar roles.
A track record of taking ambiguous, high-impact business problems from identification through measurable results.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills. You can dive into the data yourself and turn it into action.
Strong project management skills and the ability to drive execution across teams without direct authority.
Fluency with AI and automation and a strong instinct for where technology can fundamentally improve how work gets done.
Strong business judgment, low ego, high ownership, and a bias toward action.
Comfort getting into the details. This is a builder/operator role, not a strategy-only role.
Experience in a fast-growing startup is strongly preferred.
 Former founders, early-stage operators, or people who have built functions from scratch are especially compelling. 
Healthcare experience is helpful but not required.
 Why This Role Is Different 
You won’t inherit a narrow function or a fixed playbook. You’ll be expected to find the problems that matter, figure out why they exist, and own fixing them.
The goal is not better reporting. The goal is a better-performing revenue engine. 
Compensation: The expected base salary range for this role is $130,000–$200,000, depending on experience, skills, and location. This role is also eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Sales Operations Analyst

Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.
Canonical is hiring exceptional Sales Operations leaders and experienced analysts to grow and manage our global direct, alliance, channel partner and online sales. Our Sales Operations teams analyze and drive interventions to maximize net customer retention, and lead robust, repeatable processes to plan, manage and deliver revenue.
You will partner with Canonical’s executive team across sales, business development, customer success, marketing, product management, commercial systems, delivery, finance and legal and provide a focal point to drive improvements. This position requires leadership, initiative and an analytical approach, a keen eye for detail and the ability to drive continuous improvements in processes, systems, governance and data quality. People that thrive in these roles are proactive problem solvers who are passionate about the opportunity to partner with sales leadership, our role in the technology industry bringing open source to a wider audience of innovators and enterprises, and the opportunity to design and drive programs in support of Canonical's continued success.
 Location: These roles will be based remotely in the EMEA, Americas regions.

Delivering precise, scalable revenue operations for business through direct, indirect or online channels
Leading and developing a team of revenue operations analysts in developing policies, driving processes and providing daily operational support and enablement to sales teams and partners
Driving Sales Engagement, Training/Enablement/Data Enrichment, Customer Relationship Management, Configure Price Quote, Analytics and Commissions
Instrumenting, measuring and improving policies and processes across teams covering the entire revenue operations spectrum
Delivering metrics and reporting to monitor and improve revenue operations effectiveness, including new leads, pipeline, velocity, sales productivity and renewals.
Using data to drive insight, manage territories and channels, improve productivity, and agree and implement actionable change with executive management through regular sales and business reviews.
Overseeing our sales technology and processes, driving automation and process improvements and partnering with our commercial systems engineering team to continuously improve business systems and integration
Leading the introduction of new products, pricing, packaging and bundling through systems that are easy for sales and partners to navigate and quote
Driving data quality, through order processing, new hire training, process documentation, reporting and data cleansing
Leading and enhancing our commercial review process for evaluating and steering sales and alliance opportunities

What we are looking for in you
Experience operating in a leadership Revenue Operations role, driving effectiveness of direct, channel and alliance partnerships
Data-driven and analytical approach with a high attention to detail
Track record of providing insight through robust CRM and other Revenue Operations technology platforms, data, analytics, compensation systems and processes to deliver excellent revenue operations
An energetic, thoughtful, systematic approach, a problem solver with skill in measuring, identifying and delivering systems and processes that ensure repeatable, scalable outcomes
Comfort with commercial pressure, and the ability to put revenue teams under appropriate performance pressure
Organisational skills and the ability to interact and work with stakeholders within all levels of the organisation
Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
Undergraduate degree in a related field, preferably in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics or Economics, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path
Strong communication, interpersonal, negotiation and influencing skills
Professional written and spoken English with excellent presentation skills
Ability to travel internationally up to four times a year for company events up to two weeks long
Nice-to-have skills
Experience gained within a similar, technology subscription-based business
Deep understanding of working in a global, multicultural organization including driving a team based remotely in multiple time zones
Experience in mentoring and coaching team members on technical and soft skills, directly contributing to their professional development and performance improvement.
What Canonical offers
We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

title: Head of Revenue Operations
description:
Join Kainos and Shape the Future 
At Kainos, we’re problem solvers, innovators, and collaborators - driven by a shared mission to create real impact. Whether we’re transforming digital services for millions, delivering cutting-edge Workday solutions, or pushing the boundaries of technology, we do it together.
We believe in a people-first culture , where your ideas are valued, your growth is supported, and your contributions truly make a difference. Here, you’ll be part of a diverse, ambitious team that celebrates creativity and collaboration.
Ready to make your mark? Join us and be part of something bigger. 
Head of Revenue Operations 
The Head of Revenue Operations is accountable for the forecasting, data, insight, and processes that manage sales performance and inform commercial decision making across Kainos Digital Services. The role is responsible for ensuring the business has accurate, trusted and actionable insight to support business planning, target setting, forecasting, pipeline management and growth.  
Alongside these responsibilities, the role will lead the transformation of the current Sales Ops function into a broader Revenue Ops function. This represents a significant opportunity to shape how Sales, Pre-sales, Marketing, Alliances and Operations work together, establishing consistent performance management frameworks, metrics and insight across each area to improve performance, strengthen decision-making and create a more scalable go-to-market capability for Digital Services. 
A core part of the role is to establish Revenue Ops as a trusted business partnering function. Success will depend on working closely with senior stakeholders to understand their priorities and insight needs, identify sales process improvements and provide constructive challenge to drive better data-led decision-making and improve performance across the sales lifecycle. 
Key Responsibilities  
Your responsibilities will include:  
 Revenue Ops Transformation:  Define and lead transformation of the current Sales Ops function to a broader Revenue Ops capability, establishing performance management frameworks, metrics and insight across Sales, Pre-sales, Marketing and Alliances teams. Shape the future operating model for the function, including how Revenue Ops partners with each go-to-market function and the wider Digital Services business. 
 Sales Management Process & Governance:  Own and continuously improve core sales processes, including booking rules, sales order governance and the consistent treatment of contracted work, backlog and forecast demand across Digital Services. Support quota and target setting, and partner with go-to-market teams to identify and implement improvements using data, insight and seller feedback to improve sales effectiveness and forecast accuracy. 
 Forecasting, Insight and Reporting:  Own the production of reporting, forecasting and performance insights across Digital Services, spanning all go-to-market functions. Ensure leaders have accurate, timely and actionable information to support decision-making, planning, pipeline management and go-to-market performance. 
 Market Intelligence and Commercial Insight:  Lead development of our market intelligence capability, providing insight into market trends, competitor activity, customer priorities and growth opportunities, ensuring intelligence is translated into actionable recommendations that support growth priorities.  
 Data Management:  Define and maintain the standards, governance and controls  to ensure the business operates from a trusted single source of truth for data across all go-to-market functions. Proactively assure the integrity of data ensuring forecasting processes and performance reporting are underpinned by accurate, consistent and actionable data.  
 Sales Technology:  Act as the Digital Services business owner for sales technology requirements, identifying opportunities to improve sales effectiveness, operational efficiency and decision-making through better use of technology, automation and AI-enabled capabilities. Feed requirements into wider Group-level sales and marketing technology workstreams and drive effective adoption across Digital Services. 
Essential Requirements  
Significant experience in Revenue Ops, Sales Ops, Commercial Ops or a similar commercial role in a complex B2B environment.  
Proven experience running core commercial operations activities, including forecasting, commercial reporting, pipeline management, performance management, data governance and sales process improvement.  
Strong understanding of sales processes, opportunity management, forecasting methodologies, pipeline governance and commercial processes.  
Experience operating as a trusted business partner to senior stakeholders, providing insight, challenge and practical recommendations that influence commercial decisions.  
Demonstrated ability to translate complex commercial data into clear, actionable insight for executive, leadership and business review forums.  
Experience defining and governing KPIs, reporting frameworks, data standards and performance measures across commercial teams.  
Experience leading transformation activities, continuous improvement or capability development for a business function.  
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear, concise and commercially meaningful material for senior stakeholders.  
Desirable Requirements  
Experience establishing a Revenue Ops capability.  
Experience working within a technology services, consulting or SaaS B2B environment.  
Experience establishing or improving a business partnering model within a commercial, sales operations or revenue operations function.  
Experience with Microsoft Dynamics CRM and Power BI.  
Experience adopting AI, automation, Copilot, Power Platform or similar capabilities to improve sales operational efficiency and insight generation.  
Experience supporting account planning, customer lifecycle management, customer segmentation, account-based growth models or cross-functional go-to-market planning.  
Key Skills  
 Commercial Acumen:  Strong understanding of commercial drivers, contracts, forecasting, pipeline management, revenue performance and the factors that influence business growth.  
 Stakeholder Partnership and Influence:  Ability to build trusted relationships across Sales, Pre-sales, Marketing, Alliances and Operations, influencing decisions and aligning priorities across a complex organisation.  
 Strategic and Analytical Thinking:  Ability to interpret complex commercial, customer and market data, identify trends, risks and opportunities, and translate insight into practical actions that improve business performance.  
 Change and Operational Leadership:  Ability to lead operational improvement, and establish effective governance and ways of working. 
 Embracing our differences 
At Kainos, we believe in the power of diversity, equity and inclusion. We are committed to building a team that is as diverse as the world we live in, where everyone is valued, respected, and given an equal chance to thrive. We actively seek out talented people from all backgrounds, regardless of age, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or any other characteristic that makes them who they are. We also believe every candidate deserves a level playing field. 
Our friendly talent acquisition team is here to support you every step of the way, so if you require any accommodations or adjustments, we encourage you to reach out. 
We understand that everyone's journey is different, and by having a private conversation we can ensure that our recruitment process is tailored to your needs.

title: Senior Manager, Sales and Customer Success
description:
Clubspeed & Resova
Build the team. Create the playbook. Scale the customer revenue engine.
Clubspeed and Resova provide venue management, booking, and payments technology to experience-based businesses around the world.
We’re entering an exciting new chapter. With new investment behind the business, we’re building the teams, systems, and operating rhythms needed to accelerate growth while delivering a consistently strong experience for our customers.
We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Sales & Customer Success to lead that transformation across our customer segments.
The Opportunity
This is not a role where you inherit a fully built sales and customer success machine.
You’ll have the opportunity to help build it.
You’ll lead and develop a growing team responsible for customer retention, expansion, and new revenue while creating the processes, playbooks, metrics, and management structure required to operate effectively at scale.
The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. One day you may be designing the customer segmentation model or renewal process; the next, you may be coaching a rep through an expansion opportunity, reviewing an at-risk account, or helping close a deal.
You’ll have meaningful ownership over how we serve and grow our SMB and Mid-Market customers—and the opportunity to build a function that can scale with the business.
What Success Looks Like
In this role, you will:
Build a high-performing SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization with clear roles, expectations, KPIs, and accountability.
Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop a strong team of Account Managers and Customer Success professionals.
Create scalable customer journeys and playbooks across onboarding, adoption, retention, renewal, and expansion.
Improve Net Revenue Retention by reducing preventable churn and creating a consistent expansion motion across the customer base.
Establish clear forecasting and pipeline management for renewals, upsells, cross-sells, and other customer revenue opportunities.
Introduce a scalable operating model that balances high-touch engagement for strategic customers with efficient 1-to-many programs for SMB customers.
Build better visibility into customer health, revenue risk, and expansion potential.
Create a disciplined, accountable culture where the team understands what great performance looks like and has the coaching and tools to achieve it.
What You’ll DoKey Responsibilities
Lead, Build & Develop the Team
Lead the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success teams, establishing clear expectations, responsibilities, and performance standards.
Own recruiting and hiring as the organization grows.
Build structured onboarding and enablement programs that help new team members ramp quickly.
Conduct regular 1:1s, pipeline reviews, account reviews, and call coaching.
Develop the team’s capabilities in consultative selling, negotiation, customer relationship management, retention, and expansion.
Establish clear individual and team KPIs and create a strong culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
Identify performance gaps early and coach team members toward stronger outcomes.
Build the Customer Success Operating Model
Design and document scalable playbooks for onboarding, adoption, account management, renewal, expansion, and churn prevention.
Develop differentiated engagement models for SMB and Mid-Market customers based on customer value, complexity, opportunity, and risk.
Build repeatable 1-to-many programs that allow the team to effectively support a high-volume customer base.
Establish customer health scoring and early-warning indicators for churn and expansion opportunities.
Define clear escalation paths and operating processes across Sales, Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Product, and Payments.
Continuously identify opportunities to simplify workflows and improve team productivity.
Drive Retention & Expansion
Own the team’s performance against Net Revenue Retention, renewal, churn, and expansion targets.
Establish a consistent renewal process that creates visibility well in advance of contract expiration.
Build and standardize upsell and cross-sell motions across the customer base.
Coach the team on identifying customer needs, creating value-based expansion opportunities, and successfully navigating commercial conversations.
Partner with internal teams to address customer risks before they become churn events.
Step into strategic or complex customer conversations when leadership involvement can materially improve the outcome.
Create Revenue Visibility & Accountability
Build accurate weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting for renewals, expansion, and customer revenue.
Establish pipeline standards and operating rhythms that give leadership a clear view of expected performance.
Track and analyze performance metrics across the customer lifecycle.
Use product usage, customer engagement, commercial, and CRM data to identify risks and opportunities.
Ensure CRM and Customer Success systems accurately reflect account activity, pipeline, customer health, and next steps.
Provide leadership with clear insights into performance, trends, risks, and opportunities.
You’ll Thrive Here If...
You enjoy building structure where it doesn’t yet exist.
You believe strong leadership means both setting a clear standard and actively coaching people toward it.
You like working close to customers and are comfortable getting involved when an important account or opportunity needs help.
You are commercially minded and view Customer Success as an important driver of revenue, not simply a support function.
You are comfortable being accountable to clear metrics and expect the same from your team.
You can identify what needs to be standardized without adding unnecessary process.
You enjoy working in an environment where the business is evolving quickly and you can directly influence how the function develops.
You are excited by the opportunity to build something that is expected to become significantly larger over time.
Why Join Clubspeed?
This is an opportunity to join a category-leading business at an important stage of its growth.
We have an established customer base, proven products, and significant industry expertise—and we’re investing in building a stronger, more scalable commercial organization around them.
You’ll have the opportunity to:
Build and shape a critical customer-facing function.
Hire and develop your own team.
Influence how we segment, serve, retain, and grow our customers.
Work directly with company leadership on revenue strategy and execution.
Create systems and playbooks that become the foundation for future scale.
Have a measurable impact on customer retention, expansion, and company growth.
What You’ll Get
Significant ownership and autonomy over the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization.
The opportunity to build rather than simply maintain an existing function.
A seat at the table and meaningful influence over company strategy.
A growing organization where strong performers can expand their scope as the business scales.
The ability to make a visible impact on customers, employees, and company performance.
Our Hiring Process
Our hiring process is designed to be straightforward and conversational.
We want to understand how you think, how you lead, what you’ve built before, and how you would approach scaling a customer-facing revenue organization.
You’ll also have the opportunity to meet members of the leadership team, learn more about where Clubspeed and Resova are headed, and determine whether this is the right environment for you.
Join UsIf you’re excited by the opportunity to build a team, create scalable commercial processes, develop great people, and directly influence retention and growth, we’d love to hear from you.
What We’re Looking For
5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, or a related commercial function.
2+ years of direct people management or team leadership experience.
Demonstrated success hiring, onboarding, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams.
Experience operating in a high-volume SMB and/or Mid-Market environment.
Strong commercial instincts with experience managing renewals, expansion opportunities, contract negotiations, and revenue targets.
Proven ability to build processes, playbooks, operating cadences, or functions rather than simply working within established ones.
Strong understanding of Customer Success metrics including Net Revenue Retention, Gross Revenue Retention, churn, expansion, renewal rates, and customer health.
Strong forecasting, pipeline management, and performance management capabilities.
Experience using CRM and Customer Success platforms to improve visibility, automation, and team effectiveness.
Comfort working with data and translating performance metrics into concrete actions.
Ability to move between strategic planning and hands-on execution.
Competitive base+bonus compensation structure
Comprehensive health coverage, including dental and vision
Flexible time off policy

title: Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 
Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place!
As the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, you will lead two critical global pillars for Lightspeed: our Sales & Partner Commissions engine and the RevOps Capital GTM optimization & performance function. On the incentives side, you will own the end-to-end strategy, design, governance, and continuous optimization of all sales and partner commission programs, ensuring they are simple, scalable, compliant, and tightly aligned with our growth and profitability goals—while leading high-performing analyst teams to deliver accurate, timely, and trusted execution. On the RevOps Capital side, you will operate as the GTM performance “control tower,” driving forecasting, KPI frameworks, quota and coverage analytics, and weekly/monthly/quarterly business reviews that translate data into clear recommendations on investment, productivity, and commercial optimization. Partnering closely with RevOps, Finance, GTM, Legal, Enablement, and Information Systems leadership, you will ensure that every dollar we deploy in commissions and Capital programs is intentional, measurable, and focused on accelerating sustainable revenue growth and seller/partner performance globally.
 What you’ll be doing: 
 Part 1 – Global Sales & Partner Commissions 
 Program strategy, design & analytics: Own the global design, governance, and continuous improvement of sales and partner commission frameworks, using deep quantitative analysis, scenario modeling, and performance data to ensure incentives are simple, scalable, and tightly aligned with growth and profitability goals.
 Commission operations, systems & scalability: Lead end-to-end commission execution for sales and partners, ensuring payouts are accurate, timely, and aligned with contracts and plan documents; drive the transition from manual processes to scalable systems and tools, embedding robust controls, automation, and data quality.
 Insights, GTM impact & executive reporting: Turn commission and performance data into actionable insights for GTM leaders, highlighting behavioral trends, risks, and opportunities; own monthly executive readouts and presentations, delivering clear narratives and recommendations grounded in data.
 Stakeholder management & change leadership: Act as the primary RevOps point of contact for Sales, Partnerships, Finance, Legal, and IS on incentive topics; lead cross-functional changes to plan design, tooling, and processes, managing communication, enablement, and adoption across regions and teams.
 Team leadership & development: Manage, coach, and develop Sales and Partner Commissions Analysts, setting clear priorities, KPIs, and quality standards while fostering a high-performance, detail-oriented culture focused on accuracy, accountability, insights, and continuous improvement.
 Part 2 – RevOps Capital (Planning, Reporting & Performance) 
 Forecasting & reforecasting: Lead the end-to-end forecasting and reforecasting cadence for the Capital business (EOM, EOQ, EOY), refining assumptions with GTM and Finance based on macro trends, pipeline quality, and performance.
 Quota, coverage & capacity modeling: Drive quota-setting, coverage, and capacity models for Capital GTM roles, providing data-backed recommendations that align with company targets, TAM, and productivity benchmarks.
 Performance cadence (WBR/MBR/QBR): Own the weekly, monthly, and quarterly performance review cadence for Capital, bringing a “control tower” view of pipeline, bookings, portfolio metrics, and rep-level performance, and turning insights into clear actions with GTM leadership.
 KPI frameworks & strategic planning: Define and evolve KPI frameworks to measure Capital health and efficiency across the lifecycle, and translate insights into recommendations on where to invest, optimize, and improve unit economics.
 Cross-functional alignment & communication: Partner with Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Risk, and Enablement to align Capital GTM plans and reporting with company priorities; communicate complex analyses and options in clear, executive-ready narratives.
 Team & capability building: Build and mature RevOps Capital analytical capabilities, defining ways of working, tooling, and best practices, while coaching team members to strengthen strategic thinking, business acumen, and influence with senior stakeholders.
 What you need to bring: 
8-10 years in SaaS or technology, ideally in Revenue Operations, Finance, or related GTM operations roles. 4+ years of people management experience leading high-performing analytical teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Accounting or related field; Master’s is a plus.
Strong background in incentive compensation and sales/partner commissions, from design and modeling to operational execution.
Hands-on experience with forecasting, planning, and performance management in partnership with Finance and GTM leadership.
Highly analytical, process-oriented, and detail-focused, with experience using systems/tools (commission platforms, CRM, BI) to scale operations.
Excellent communication and executive presence, with a track record of presenting insights and recommendations to senior leadership; experience in Financial Services or Capital products is a plus.
As a global company with employees and clients outside of Quebec, fluency in English as a working language is required for this position
 What will make you successful: 
 Exceptional analytical & quantitative skills: You’re comfortable deep in spreadsheets, models, and dashboards, turning complex performance and commission data into clear, actionable insights.
 Strategic systems thinker: You can zoom out to design scalable frameworks for incentives, forecasting, and performance management, while staying close enough to the details to spot risks and edge cases.
 Clear, confident communicator: You can explain complex commission logic, trade-offs, and Capital performance insights to executives and front-line teams in simple, compelling language.
 Change leadership & influence: You’re skilled at driving adoption of new plans, tools, and processes across GTM, Finance, Legal, and IS, building buy-in rather than just enforcing rules.
 Operator mindset & bias for action: You care about accuracy and control, but you also move fast—constantly looking for ways to streamline, automate, and improve how the work gets done.
 Collaborative team player: You build strong relationships across functions and regions, balancing partner/revenue goals with governance, compliance, and operational feasibility.
 People leadership & talent development: You enjoy coaching analytical talent, setting clear expectations, giving feedback, and building a high-performance culture grounded in ownership and accountability.
We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!
 Be a changemaker 
You’ll enjoy:
A flexible work environment that empowers you to do your best work
A culture that celebrates performance
The chance to make an impact in a team that’s big enough for career growth, but lean enough to make your voice heard
Career-defining opportunities
Plus benefits designed to keep you happy, healthy and fulfilled.
Flexible paid time off and remote work policies
Equity options, because this is your company too
Contributions to your pension plan. Your future matters
Training opportunities to grow your skills and career
Health and wellness credit so you feel your best
Time off to volunteer and give back to your community
Interest groups, employee led networks, social committees to sponsored sports teams
Computer purchase program to get your personal Macbook
Enhanced parental leave to support growing families
Fuel your growth. Find your people.
At Lightspeed, your growth is our priority. We invest in you with continuous learning opportunities, global mobility and benefits designed to support you—all within a driven, diverse and inclusive team that’s passionate about empowering our communities
 Final thought... Studies show that gender-coded words significantly reduce the number of women applying. Use this link to find out if your job description is gender-neutral: http://gender-decoder.katmatfield.com/
 || ONLY IF CRIMINAL CHECK APPLIES || Please note that we ask applicants to disclose any criminal convictions, and we conduct criminal record checks as part of our hiring process for this role. 
 #LI-TL2
 To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. 
 Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. 
 Where to from here? 
Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.
Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.
 Who we are: 
Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.
Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

title: Sr. Manager, Commercial Incentives & Revenue Operations
description:
At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.
Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work.  What you'll do 
 Own VIP (Variable Incentive Plan)Plan Design, Impact Modeling & Governance

Coordinate directly with Legal, Local Geo/Works Council teams, Finance, and Employee Communications as needed for VIP plan implementation.
Own the overall communication plan for VIP and commercial program changes. Communicate program vision and impact to senior leadership and wider organisation with clarity and confidence.
 Own and Evolve the Sales Operating Model 
Lead and partner with Sales Leaders and HR to define the evolution of the Sales Blueprint and Operating Framework, defining roles, competencies, KPIs, and actions that underpin sales excellence.
Lead the ongoing refinement, adoption, and execution of partner Tier Segmentation, ensuring clear differentiation of priorities, resourcing, and commercial approach, and driving consistent application across sales teams.
Drive adoption of the blueprint and sales frameworks across regions, embedding them into onboarding, coaching, and performance management.
Act as the connector between strategy and execution, ensuring sales excellence and VIP design are lived consistently across teams and regions.
 Lead Strategic Sales Excellence Initiatives 
Identify and lead complex, cross-functional programs that enhance sales performance and scalability, defining scope, governance, milestones, and success metrics.
Mobilize and influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Product, Legal, Finance, HR, and Commercial Operations.
Use data and AI to define KPIs, track sales excellence and VIP program effectiveness, and identify opportunities to simplify reporting and speed up decisions.
 Who you are 
Strong program management and execution skills.
Experience on incentive plan design and employee impact modeling desired.
Experience navigating formal governance processes for any employee related changes.
Strong track record leading sales excellence, enablement, or commercial strategy programs at scale.
Comfortable operating at Senior Manager level: representing the function to senior stakeholders (VP+) with autonomy and minimal oversight.
AI-savvy and data-literate; confident using AI tools and data to shape design decisions, not just report on them.
Skilled at navigating cross-functional ambiguity across Sales, HR/Compensation, Legal, Finance, and Comms
Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or related field; Travel or B2B SaaS experience preferred.
The total cash range for this position in Madrid is €70,000.00 to €98,000.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to €112,000.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role.
Starting pay for this role will vary based on multiple factors, including location, available budget, and an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience. Pay ranges may be modified in the future.
 Benefits and perks 
Expedia Group offers benefits and perks designed to support employees and their families, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, an Employee Assistance Program, wellness and travel reimbursement, travel discounts, and International Airlines Travel Agent Network (IATAN) membership. Learn more about life at Expedia Group at https://careers.expediagroup.com/life .
 You can find the benefits for this location and any collective agreement that may apply here .

 About Expedia Group 
Expedia Group includes three flagship consumer brands - Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo - along with a leading B2B travel business and travel advertising offerings. Across our brands and business, we help travelers explore the world with confidence and ease.

Employment opportunities and job offers at Expedia Group will always come from Expedia Group's Talent Acquisition and hiring teams. title: Head of Revenue Operations & Systems
description:
We power people’s progress. 
At Preply, we’re all about creating life-changing learning experiences. We help people discover the magic of the perfect tutor, craft a personalised learning journey, and stay motivated to keep growing. Our approach is human-led, tech-enabled - and it’s creating real impact.
We’ve just reached unicorn status with a $150M Series D, accelerating our vision to transform education through human-led, AI-enhanced learning. Today, 100,000+ tutors teach 90+ languages to learners in 180 countries - and we’re only getting started. As a category-defining company, we’re shaping what the future of learning looks like at global scale.
Every Preply lesson sparks change, fuels ambition, and drives progress that matters. Joining Preply means helping define the future of education at global scale, and building something that truly matters for millions of people, every day.
 Meet the team! 
This new team will design, scale, and future-proof the systems and automation that power Preply’s revenue engine. You’ll blend hands-on system expertise with strategic ownership - building scalable, integrated processes while leading a small, high-performing team to drive efficiency, data accuracy, and innovation across our GTM stack.
This is a hybrid role: part architect and builder, part strategic manager who aligns tools, data, and teams to accelerate growth, transforming RevOps from reactive operations to proactive scalability. The exciting part - lead a fast-moving, ambitious team that values precision, autonomy, and continuous improvement, plus the opportunity to build and shape the next-generation GTM infrastructure that powers global growth.
What You’ll Be Doing:
 1. Systems Ownership & Architecture 
Own the design, optimization, and health of Preply’s GTM system landscape Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, Vitally, Intercom, and connected tools.
Partner with cross-functional teams (Marketing Ops, Pre Sales, Sales, CS, Finance, Product) to ensure integrations are seamless and scalable.
Lead the evolution of system architecture — mapping processes, maintaining clean data structures, and reducing technical debt.
Drive adoption of new GTM tools through documentation, enablement, and user-friendly workflows.
 2. Automation & Process Optimization

Implement AI-assisted and no-code automation to streamline pipeline operations and reduce manual effort.
Build standardized playbooks and process documentation to ensure repeatable, reliable execution across teams.
Partner with Enablement to roll out new tools and processes with clear training and adoption metrics.
 3. Data Integrity & Insights Infrastructure 
Own data accuracy and governance across CRM and connected systems.
Build and maintain self-serve dashboards (Salesforce, Looker) to visualize funnel metrics, forecasting, churn, and pipeline velocity.
Deliver strategic data insights to senior leadership to inform GTM decisions.
Partner with StratOps to ensure data models support forecasting, compensation, and territory planning.
 4. Tooling Strategy & Vendor Management 
Manage the GTM tooling roadmap, budget, and vendor relationships.
Evaluate new technologies and AI integrations that enhance productivity, personalization, and insight generation.
Ensure ROI and strategic alignment of all tools — balancing innovation with practicality.
 5. Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration 
Lead and mentor a small team of system specialists or analysts, fostering curiosity, precision, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, and CS stakeholders to translate business requirements into scalable system solutions.
Champion “system thinking” across GTM — ensuring clarity, consistency, and documentation in how we operate. 
What You Need to Succeed:
8+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, or Sales/Marketing Ops in a fast-scaling B2B SaaS environment.
Deep technical expertise in Salesforce (architecture, admin, and automation).
Strong understanding of GTM processes and data flows (lead-to-opportunity, opportunity-to-renewal).
Experience with BI and reporting tools (Looker, Tableau, Google Data Studio).
Proven ability to translate business,user and customer needs into technical solutions.
Familiarity with no-code automation tools (Zapier, Workato, n8n) and API integrations.
Experience leading teams and leading cross-functional initiatives.
Excellent communication and stakeholder alignment skills — comfortable bridging technical and commercial conversations.
Strong analytical mindset and attention to detail, balanced with pragmatism and speed.
 Why you’ll love it at Preply: 
An open, collaborative, dynamic and diverse culture;
A generous monthly allowance for lessons on Preply.com , Learning & Development budget and time off for your self-development;
A competitive financial package with equity, leave allowance and health insurance;
Access to free mental health support platforms;
Access to Gympass-partnered wellness and gym centers to promote and support well-being and physical health;

 A Bit About The Role
 In this role you will be responsible for designing and building the systems that power the Wise Business go-to-market engine.  About IFS Copperleaf 
IFS Copperleaf builds decision analytics and capital planning software for the organisations that run critical infrastructure: electric, gas and water utilities, transportation and rail, oil and gas, mining, and the public sector. Our software helps asset-intensive companies decide where and when to invest, balancing cost, risk, performance and sustainability, and it is used today to manage more than $2.9 trillion of assets worldwide.
These are high-stakes, evidence-led sales. Our buyers, CFOs, VPs of Asset Management, chief engineers and capital planning leaders, answer to regulators, boards and rate cases. title: Senior Director, Business Management, Strategy & Revenue Operations, Institutional Solutions
description:
Can you build the commercial operating foundations for a growing B2B business? Do you know what strong Revenue Operations looks like before the systems, processes and rhythms are fully mature? Are you at your best when strategy, execution, governance and stakeholder influence all need to come together?
At CFA Institute, we are building the B2B commercial foundations for Institutional Solutions. As Senior Director, Business Management, Strategy & Revenue Operations, Institutional Solutions , you will help shape how we define, manage and scale direct institutional relationships, bringing structure to a growing global commercial motion.
This is a build role. You will not simply inherit a fully mature operating model. You will help design the foundations: customer segmentation, opportunity definitions, pipeline discipline, forecasting, revenue management, sales playbooks, governance and the future shape of the RevOps function.
What You’ll Do
Build the foundational Revenue Operations architecture for CFA Institute’s growing B2B institutional business, including segmentation, opportunity definitions, sales playbook foundations, pipeline discipline and forecasting rhythms
Translate Institutional Solutions strategy into scalable operating models, governance, performance routines and practical execution plans
Lead the design and implementation of commercial enablement foundations, including sales compensation and revenue management processes
Act as a senior internal partner to the Managing Director, representing the division in cross-functional discussions with Finance, Legal, People & Culture and other enabling teams
Shape the future RevOps team, deciding which capabilities to build first and how to resource the function effectively
Move the function from early-stage build into steady-state business management across pipeline, goals, forecasting, revenue and performance outcomes
What We’re Looking For
Proven B2B Revenue Operations experience, ideally in a SaaS, fintech, education, professional learning or similarly complex commercial environment
Experience building or scaling commercial operating foundations such as customer segmentation, sales playbooks, opportunity qualification, pipeline management, forecasting or sales compensation
Strong strategy-to-execution capability, with evidence of turning ambiguous business needs into prioritised plans and delivered outcomes
International or global operating exposure, with awareness of how market, currency, tax or regional complexity can affect commercial operations
Senior stakeholder credibility and the confidence to influence across Finance, Legal, People & Culture, commercial teams and leadership forums
People leadership or team-build experience, including the ability to define future capability needs in a growing function
A self-starter mindset, comfortable owning problems where the foundations are not yet fully built
Why Join Us
Build the commercial operating foundations for a strategically important new division at CFA Institute
Take on a rare zero-to-one RevOps build with the backing, access and brand strength of a global professional body
Work closely with senior leadership on business model, governance, performance and commercial execution decisions
Shape how CFA Institute develops direct institutional relationships and scales its B2B motion globally
Join a lean, high-trust environment where your judgement, pace and ownership will directly shape outcomes
At CFA Institute, we are committed to transparency and equity in our hiring process. Compensation for this role will be determined based on experience, education, and other factors relevant to the position. Additional benefits include eligibility for an annual incentive bonus, a 12% employer contribution to a pension plan, and a comprehensive medical benefits package. .
We offer a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees, including health coverage, generous time off, competitive retirement plans, flexible work options, and wellbeing and development programs. You can learn more on our careers site: Working at CFA Institute | Comprehensive Benefits
 About CFA Institute
 CFA Institute is the global leader in investment excellence and ethics. With nearly 200,000 charterholders across 160 markets, we promote professional growth, uphold ethical standards, and help advance better financial markets. Join a global organization committed to putting investors first.
Follow CFA Institute on: LinkedIn | YouTube | Facebook | Instagram | WeChat | Weibo
 Important Message: Your application must clearly demonstrate how you meet the requirements as CFA Institute cannot make assumptions about your education, experience, or location. We thank all those who apply. 
 We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. CFA Institute prohibits both discrimination and harassment with regard to all identifying characteristics: any individual employee, group of employees, or prospective employee on the basis of race, color, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, religion, creed or belief, age, marital or partnership status, marital or family status, care giver status, pregnancy and maternity, sexual and other reproductive health decisions, physical abilities/qualities, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, predisposing genetic characteristic, military or veteran status, status as a victim or witness of domestic violence or sex offense or stalking, unemployment status, infectious disease carrier status, migrant worker status, educational background, socio-economic status, geographic location and culture or any other basis protected by applicable law. This policy impacts all aspects of employment, including but not limited to, recruitment, hiring, compensation, training, development, promotion, demotion, layoff, recall, furlough, transfer, leave of absence, and dismissal. This is a global policy that applies to all CFA Institute employees, regardless of location.
